zupmxio

A population PK/PD model often has to move between tools: a NONMEM run becomes an nlmixr2 model for a new analysis, or an mrgsolve model for simulation. Converters exist, but a translated model is usually trusted on sight, and a slip in a volume or a residual model shows up much later, if at all.

zupmxio makes the translation checkable. It reads a model from NONMEM, rxode2/nlmixr2 or mrgsolve into one R object, writes it to any of the three, and proves that two models are the same model by simulating both and comparing their predictions.

  • The check is the product. pmx_compare() simulates both models on a canonical design (single dose, infusion, multiple doses and steady state, for a typical subject and subjects with random effects) and reports the worst deviation against a tolerance. A failed comparison is a result that says where the models differ, not an error.
  • Independent engines. Each model runs on its own engine, rxode2 or mrgsolve, and never on the engine of the writer under test, so a translation is not checked by the code that made it.
  • Nothing is guessed. Code outside the supported subset is refused with its position. A writer that would drop something that changes predictions refuses the model, and every write reports its fidelity: exact, equivalent or lossy, with what was lost.
  • Against NONMEM’s own output. pmx_compare() also takes the tables a NONMEM run wrote, and checks a translation against the run’s PRED.
  • A corpus with oracles. Every shipped model is checked against nonmem2rx and, for ODE models, amp.sim.

Installation

Install zupmxio from CRAN:

install.packages("zupmxio")

Or the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("pedrobtz/zupmxio")

zupmxio itself has no dependencies. Comparisons need the engines, rxode2 and mrgsolve, which need a C and C++ compiler to build models.

Usage 

library(zupmxio)

Read a model. This one is a two-compartment model with first-order absorption, from the corpus that ships with the package:

path <- system.file("corpus", "twocmt-oral", "model.ctl", package = "zupmxio")
model <- pmx_read_nonmem(path)
model
#> <zupmxio_model> read from nonmem
#> Structure: two-compartment closed form, first-order input (ADVAN4 TRANS4)
#> Parameters: 5, initial values only
#> Random effects: ETA1 on CL (exp), ETA2 on V2 (exp)
#> Endpoints: Y (proportional)

Write it to rxode2. The fidelity says the translation is a known reparameterisation, here residual error as a standard deviation rather than a variance:

rx <- pmx_write_rxode2(model)
pmx_fidelity(rx)
#> [1] "equivalent"

Check it. The NONMEM model runs on mrgsolve and the rxode2 text runs as written, on rxode2, and every one of the predictions agrees:

pmx_compare(model, rx)
#> <zupmxio comparison> pass
#> a: nonmem model, written to mrgsolve by zupmxio, on mrgsolve 2.0.1
#> b: rxode2 text, simulated as written, on rxode2 5.1.8
#> Tolerance: relative 1e-06, absolute 1e-09.
#> 0 of 735 predictions disagree.
#> Worst: ss, subject 15, time 0.5: 4.4041147 against 4.4041147 (abs 6.06e-10, rel 1.38e-10).
#>   regimen points failed  max_abs  max_rel skipped
#>    single    168      0 1.02e-14 8.11e-15        
#>  infusion    168      0 8.44e-15 7.44e-15        
#>  multiple    252      0 1.60e-14 8.68e-15        
#>        ss    147      0 6.06e-10 1.79e-10

A slip fails. Here the central volume of the rxode2 text is 21 instead of 20, and the comparison says where the predictions part:

slip <- rx
slip$text <- sub("THETA3 <- c(0, 20)", "THETA3 <- c(0, 21)", slip$text, fixed = TRUE)
pmx_compare(model, slip)
#> <zupmxio comparison> FAIL
#> a: nonmem model, written to mrgsolve by zupmxio, on mrgsolve 2.0.1
#> b: rxode2 text, simulated as written, on rxode2 5.1.8
#> Tolerance: relative 1e-06, absolute 1e-09.
#> 735 of 735 predictions disagree.
#> Worst: infusion, subject 5, time 8: 0.26833057 against 0.28530119 (abs 0.017, rel 0.0595).
#>   regimen points failed max_abs max_rel skipped
#>    single    168    168   0.125  0.0592        
#>  infusion    168    168   0.102  0.0595        
#>  multiple    252    252   0.125  0.0587        
#>        ss    147    147   0.119  0.0404

pmx_report() writes a comparison as Markdown, with the design, the deviations and both model texts, for a reviewer to read without running anything.

Functions are named by what they do: pmx_read_*() and pmx_write_*() for each format, and pmx_design(), pmx_compare() and pmx_report() for the check.

Learn more

  • Validating a translation walks through a check end to end, and shows how to read a report.
  • The reference lists the readers, the writers and the comparison functions.
  • zupmxio_corpus() lists the shipped models.

Related work

zupmxio is checked against nonmem2rx, which translates NONMEM to rxode2, and amp.sim, which translates it to mrgsolve; oracle-agreement.md records where they agree. The nlmixr2lib model library is read in its tests. Its tables and run files are read with zucsv and zuxml when installed.
